sections.title: Index Overview
sections.intro: The S&P 500 is designed to represent the US large-cap equity market. Constituents are screened from the S&P Total Market Index, with the Index Committee making the final inclusion decisions.
bullets: It is not a mechanical ranking of the top 500 by market cap; committee judgment and sector-balance constraints apply.
The goal is to cover the US large-cap segment while preserving investability and tradability.

sections.title: Eligibility
sections.intro: Candidates must first clear hard thresholds before entering the committee's final consideration set.
bullets: Must be a US-domiciled company that meets US securities disclosure requirements.
Must list on a qualifying US exchange such as NYSE, Nasdaq, or Cboe BZX/EDGX.
The legal structure is typically a corporation, and the security type is typically common stock.
The current company-level market cap threshold for the S&P 500 is above $22.7 billion, with the security-level float-adjusted market cap at least 50% of that threshold.
At addition, the liquidity test requires at least 250,000 shares traded each month over the prior six months, and the FALR must be no lower than 0.75.
Financially, GAAP net income from continuing operations must be positive in the most recent quarter and in the sum of the trailing four quarters.

sections.title: Additions and Deletions
sections.intro: The index is not rebalanced wholesale each quarter; it is mostly event-driven and committee-maintained.
bullets: The Index Committee has final discretion: clearing the thresholds does not guarantee inclusion.
Sector balance is considered, with reference to GICS sector weights within the relevant market-cap range of the S&P Total Market Index.
M&A, delistings, bankruptcies, and corporate restructurings frequently trigger constituent replacements.
Former SPACs typically need 12 months of trading history after de-SPAC before being considered.

sections.title: Weights and Maintenance
sections.intro: The S&P 500 is neither equal-weighted nor price-weighted, but float-adjusted market-cap weighted.
bullets: Weight is determined by a company's investable market cap; share count, IWF, and price all influence the weight.
Index maintenance is continuous in response to corporate actions, share changes, and constituent replacements.
Market-cap thresholds are reviewed quarterly; if the ranges drift too far, the committee updates the large/mid/small-cap cutoffs.
